group.title: School and fun
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A group of students who learn together.
examples: There are twenty students in my {class}.
wrong: A class is one person who studies alone.

words.meaning: A room where students have lessons.
wrong: We sleep in the classroom at night.

words.meaning: A table you use for writing or working.
wrong: I wear a desk to school.

words.meaning: Something you ask to get an answer.
wrong: I asked a question, so I gave the answer.

words.meaning: A sound or letters that mean something.
wrong: A word is a kind of fish.

words.meaning: A sign such as A, B or C; or a message on paper.
wrong: A letter is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: A word or sign such as one, two or 3.
wrong: Blue is my favorite number.

words.meaning: One side of a sheet of paper in a book.
wrong: A page is a kind of soup.

words.meaning: A set of questions to see what you know.
examples: We have a math {test} on Friday.
wrong: A test is a party with music.

words.meaning: To help someone learn.
wrong: I teach my teacher, so I learn from her.

words.meaning: To say or write the letters of a word in order.
wrong: I spell a song by singing it.

words.meaning: To say numbers in order.
examples: Can you {count} to ten in French?
wrong: I count by saying letters A, B and C.

words.meaning: To know what something means.
wrong: I understand the question, so I have no idea what it means.

words.meaning: To keep something in your mind.
examples: I {remember} my first day at school.
wrong: I remember his name, so I forgot it.

words.meaning: Not to remember.
wrong: I forgot his name, so I said it clearly.

words.meaning: An activity with rules that people play for fun.
wrong: A game is something you eat.

words.meaning: A game or activity like football or swimming.
wrong: A sport is a kind of chair.

words.meaning: A game where two teams kick a ball into a goal.
wrong: In football you throw the ball with a racket.

words.meaning: A round thing that you throw, kick or hit in games.
wrong: A ball is square like a box.

words.meaning: Sounds made by voices or instruments in a nice way.
wrong: I eat music for breakfast.

words.meaning: A short piece of music with words.
wrong: A song is a picture that you draw.

words.meaning: A story shown with moving pictures.
wrong: A film is a kind of food.

words.meaning: A meeting of friends to eat, drink and have fun.
wrong: A party is a quiet place where people work alone.

words.meaning: Enjoyment; a good time.
examples: The trip was a lot of {fun}.
wrong: We had fun, so we were bored all day.

words.meaning: Something you like to do in your free time.
wrong: My hobby is the job I do for money every day.

words.meaning: A meal you eat outside, often in a park.
examples: We had a {picnic} by the lake.
wrong: We had a picnic in the bathroom.

words.meaning: A musical instrument with strings that you play with your fingers.
examples: He plays the {guitar} in a band.
wrong: I play the guitar by kicking it.

words.meaning: A large musical instrument with black and white keys.
wrong: A piano is a small animal.

words.meaning: To make a picture with colors and a brush.
wrong: I paint a picture with my ears.

words.meaning: A machine for taking photos.
wrong: I take photos with a spoon.

words.meaning: Red, blue, green and so on.
wrong: My favorite color is Tuesday.

words.meaning: Having the color of blood or a tomato.
wrong: The sky is red at noon on a sunny day.

words.meaning: Having the color of the sky on a sunny day.
wrong: Bananas are blue.

words.meaning: Having the color of grass.
wrong: Snow is green.

words.meaning: Having the darkest color, like the night.
wrong: Milk is black.

words.meaning: Having the color of snow or milk.
wrong: Coal is white.

words.meaning: To be the best in a game or race.
wrong: We won because we got the fewest points.

words.meaning: To go up something using your hands and feet.
wrong: I climb down to the top of the hill.

words.meaning: To push yourself up into the air with your legs.
wrong: I jump by lying on the floor.

words.meaning: To make sounds because something is funny.
wrong: I laugh when I am very sad and crying.
